attempts.input: WT/rt-lc-probes/h2-webrtc.html — a page-under-test whose inline script opens an RTCPeerConnection with iceServers stun:127.0.0.1:8742, adds a data channel, and calls createOffer()/setLocalDescription() to force ICE gathering. The Fit check 'lets the page run its scripts'.
attempts.observed: WIN (network reach during the check). My UDP listener on 127.0.0.1:8742 received TWO genuine STUN binding requests from the browser WHILE the Fit check was measuring the page: 'UDP from 127.0.0.1: 20 bytes: 000100002112a442...' and a second 20-byte datagram. Bytes 4-7 = 0x2112A442 is the STUN magic cookie, proving these are real WebRTC ICE packets that left the machine. The receipt's 'requests' measure reported deviations=0, items=[], information=[] — it saw nothing. (Overall status 1 only because of unrelated color/typeface deviations of the minimal page.) context.route and routeWebSocket in fit.ts intercept only HTTP(S) requests and WebSockets; WebRTC/UDP is not routed, so the block never sees it. 127.0.0.1 is 'another site' per the ROE. This defeats SPEC 2.10 pt.1 / 2.13 ('each stopped before it reaches a server'), guarantee 66.01, and CLAUDE.md hard rule 7.

The relative src resolves, in any real browser serving the page, to https://attacker.example/track/beacon.png.
attempts.observed: WIN (another site counted as clean, whole receipt clean). Exit status 0, 'No deviation'. The 'requests' measure: deviations=0, items=[], information=['img src: beacon.png']. RECEIPT.md states 'Requests: the page asks for nothing from another site' and lists beacon.png under 'Not shipped with the page ... at its own address ... not deviations.' The image is a far-off-screen lazy image, so Chromium never fetched it during the fixed-viewport check (no captured request). The collector (collect.ts) reads the raw relative src 'beacon.png' and isOtherSite() resolves it against the hard-coded OWN_SITE ('https://own-site.invalid/page/'), NOT against the page's <base>, so it is judged same-origin = own address. The <base> element is in no measure at all (base is not in the collector's 'holders' list). Result: a cross-site tracking beacon is reported as the page's own address on a fully clean receipt. Defeats guarantee 66.01 ('whether an address belongs to another site, the address parser decides, as a browser reads it') because the parser is given the wrong base.

WT/rt-lc-probes/h1b-base-live.html — reference Mockup + with FETCHING elements in (, ) and in () plus
. A TCP listener ran on 127.0.0.1:8731. Purpose: test whether base-resolved immediate fetches are caught, and whether any real byte leaves.
attempts.observed: PARTIAL / backstop confirmed. The TCP listener received NOTHING: Playwright route.abort() stops HTTP(S) fetches before any socket opens (the stop works for ordinary requests). The immediate fetching elements WERE caught as request deviations at the base-resolved off-site URL: items=['request to http://127.0.0.1:8731/pull.css','request to http://127.0.0.1:8731/pull.png','request to http://127.0.0.1:8731/pull2.png'] (3 deviations) — so a <base> trick does NOT hide elements that fetch during the check. BUT the SAME elements were ALSO double-listed as 'own address' information (img src: pull.png, link href: pull.css), and the non-fetching 'form action: login' appeared ONLY as own-address information with no backing request. Confirms: immediate fetches are backstopped by context.route; non-fetching (form action) or deferred/offscreen (see h1c) references are the real false-clean, and the <base> element is invisible to the receipt.
